# OwnerFlight — Full Text

OwnerFlight books calls with home care agency owners for businesses that sell into home care — done-for-you outreach backed by a scored database of 11,540 agencies across 24 live states (The Deal $800 one-time, DFY $1,500/mo, DIY database $299/mo for any 3 states, All-Access $499/mo for every live state, DFY annual prepaid $15,000/year).

What We Do
Your pipeline problem isn't your offer. It's reaching the owners.
Home care agency owners don't sit on LinkedIn waiting for pitches. They're running caregivers, covering shifts, and answering families. OwnerFlight was built to reach them where they actually are — and to keep working the conversation until it's a booked call or a clear no.

Questions
Before you ask.
Who is this for?
Any business that sells to home care agency owners — software, staffing, billing, consulting, franchising, senior placement, and the agencies' own vendors. If your buyers are agency owners, this is your front door to them.
What exactly happens after I pay?
You tell us your market and what you sell. We confirm the exact owner count for that market in writing, draft the outreach angle for your approval, then run the flight. Replies land in real conversations; interested owners get booked on your calendar with their name, agency, and what they said.
Which channels do you use?
All of them: WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, email, and text — matched to how each owner actually responds. Outreach sends from our accounts, never your domain or your phone number.
What counts as a positive reply?
An owner showing any interest in talking — asking a question, asking for information, agreeing to a call. Wrong numbers, gatekeepers, and clear no's don't count, and you'll see every reply either way in your weekly report.
Why only 10 deal spots?
Every flight is worked by people, reply by reply. Ten deals is what we can run properly at once. When the 10 are gone, the Deal is gone — the standing way in is DFY at $1,500/mo.
Can I see the data first?
Yes — the sample page shows the record format, and the exact owner count for your market is confirmed in writing before anything sends.
Your buyers are owners. We get you in front of them.
First 10 deal spots only — when they're gone, they're gone.

Why bought lists fail
You have bought this list before. It did not work then either.
The standard list-buying experience — pay per record, get a spreadsheet, start dialing — breaks in the same three places every time.
01 / STALE
Dead on arrival
Most lists are scraped once and resold for years. Agencies close, rebrand, move, and change administrators — and the spreadsheet never hears about any of it. Your first week of outreach becomes a cleanup project.
02 / NO OWNER
A name, not a person
A business name and a front-desk number is not a lead. Without the owner or administrator — cross-checked against the state license record — your reps pitch whoever answers the phone and hope it travels upward.
03 / NO TIMING
No reason to call today
A flat list treats a fast-growing agency and a dormant one as identical rows. Nothing in it says who has a visible problem a marketer can fix this week — so every call starts cold, in every sense.
Here is what the Florida market actually looks like when you verify it record by record — this gap is the opportunity, and it is invisible in a bought list:
Online booking
19 of 32
Florida agencies verified so far show an online booking path — the other 13 verified are phone-only in a market where families shop online first. Statewide verification is still in progress; we publish only what we've checked.
Instagram
99 of 102
have no findable Instagram presence at all. Only 3 agencies in the entire statewide file show one.
Reviews
Median: 10
Google reviews for the typical rated Florida agency. Reputation volume is thin almost everywhere — a fixable, sellable gap.
Email — DFY's layer
48 of 102
Florida records carry a verified, published email address — the contact layer our DFY team emails from. Emails aren't in the DIY file; DIY is owners, phones, licenses and scores, built for calling.

FAQ
Straight answers, before you subscribe.
Where can I buy a list of home care agencies?
OwnerFlight is a subscription database of licensed home care agencies, built for marketing agencies: 11,540 verified records across 24 live states — owner names, direct phones, and license numbers where verified, plus ratings, booking and social signals, and a priority score on every record. It is $299/month, and the $800 Deal proves it in your market before you subscribe. Twenty-four states are live — 11,540 agencies, Florida to Colorado — and DIY includes your choice of three states ($299/month); All-Access includes all 24 states ($499/month) with no hidden per-record fees.
Are these leads exclusive to my agency?
No — and we would rather say that plainly. OwnerFlight is a shared subscription database: every member works from the same verified file. What members compete on is speed and follow-up, and the weekly Hot 10 and its timing signals are built to give you that edge. If a vendor promises exclusive leads at this price, ask how many times they have sold them.
What information comes with each agency?
Thirteen core fields: agency name, city, street address, phone, website, state license number, owner or administrator, Google rating and review count, Instagram handle and recent activity, online-booking signal, priority score, tier, and a plain-English reason for the score. Fields that can’t be verified are left blank, never estimated. One honest gap: this file doesn’t include email addresses. Verified owner emails live in DFY — the tier where we do the emailing for you. DIY is owners, phones, licenses and scores, built for calling.
How fresh is the data?
The Florida file was verified record by record in October 2026, against state license records and each agency's live web presence. The full database is re-verified and refreshed every week, and the Hot 10 brief goes out every Monday with the highest-priority accounts and what changed.
Which states are covered?
Twenty-four states are live — 11,540 agencies, Florida to Colorado — and DIY includes your choice of three states ($299/month); All-Access includes all 24 states ($499/month). Whatever rate you start at is yours for as long as you stay subscribed.

Senior-care signals
Online-booking gaps, Instagram presence and activity, Google rating and review counts, and a 0–100 priority score with the plain-English reason on every row
Generic firmographic and technographic data; senior-care prospecting signals like booking gaps are not the product

FAQ
The comparison questions, answered straight.
How is OwnerFlight different from Apollo or ZoomInfo?
Broad B2B platforms are built to cover every industry. OwnerFlight is built around one vertical — 11,540 licensed home care agencies across 24 live states — and includes license numbers plus senior-care-specific prospecting signals, such as visible Instagram activity and online-booking gaps, that broad databases typically do not carry.
How does the pricing compare?
OwnerFlight publishes flat prices with self-serve Stripe checkout: a $800 one-time The Deal, Done-For-You at $1,500/mo, and the DIY database at $299/mo (any 3 states), plus All-Access — every live state — at $499/mo. Apollo and ZoomInfo sell per-seat contracts, typically quote-only.
Which one has verified home care owner emails?
OwnerFlight's Done-For-You tier works from verified owner emails across the 24 live states, and we run the outreach for you. Verified owner emails are DFY-only; the DIY database is owners, phones, licenses, and scores.

How it works
Three steps. No integration project, no cookie arguments.
Tracking is deliberately simple: a personal partner code, logged in our subscriber registry at signup. If a signup names your code, it is yours — permanently, and auditable any time you ask.
01
Get your partner code
Email us and tell us about your audience. We issue your personal code and walk you through the file, so you only promote what you have actually seen.
02
Share the data or the offer
Publish the market findings, share the $800 Deal, host a session, or link the database — always with your code attached and your commission disclosed.
03
Earn every month, for life
Commissions tally monthly and pay out via Stripe once your balance passes $100 — 10% on DIY subscriptions ($29.90/mo each), 25% on DFY clients ($375/mo each) — and keep paying for as long as each subscriber stays subscribed.
Partner conduct
Simple rules, enforced.
The whole product is trust in data. Partners protect that — and their commission — by following three rules. The full terms arrive with your partner code, before you promote anything.
Rule 01
Honest claims only
Cite the published brief and the live coverage — 24 states are live today. Never promise states, features, or results we have not shipped.
Rule 02
Disclose the commission
A simple “I may earn a commission” line wherever you promote. FTC basics — it protects you, us, and your audience's trust in both.
Rule 03
No spam, ever
No purchased lists, no mass unsolicited outreach, no posting your code where you do not have permission to promote. One spam complaint ends the partnership.

2026 Data Brief · Florida
The State of Florida Home Care, in numbers.
We analyzed 102 licensed Florida home care agencies — their websites, booking paths, social presence, and Google profiles. The headline: this is a large, licensed, paying market that is almost completely invisible online.
Data collected & verified October 2026 · OwnerFlight research
19 / 32 verified agencies offer any online booking Booking status is verified agency by agency against each agency's own site. Of the 32 verified so far, 19 offer online booking and 13 are phone-only. The rest are still being verified — we publish only what we've checked.
99 / 102 have no findable Instagram presence Just 3 agencies in the entire dataset have an Instagram profile we could find. The channel families actually browse is essentially empty.
10 median Google reviews per rated agency Ratings average a strong 4.8★ — but on a median of 10 reviews, one unhappy family moves the number. High ratings, thin proof.
102 licensed agencies, verified one by one Built from Florida license records, cross-checked against each agency's live web presence. Unverifiable fields are left blank — never estimated.
Where the agencies are
The dataset concentrates in Florida's major metros — the same metros where private-pay demand and agency competition are highest:
Jacksonville · 14 Miami · 13 Orlando · 8 Tampa · 7 Altamonte Springs · 7 St. Petersburg · 6 Kissimmee · 5 Orange Park · 5
What this means if you sell marketing to home care agencies
The booking gap is a web & intake pitch, pre-written
13 of the 32 agencies verified so far can't take a booking or consultation request online. Every one is flagged individually in the database — that's not a cold list, it's 13 warm reasons to call, with more verifying every week.
Social silence is a content pitch with no competition
When 97% of a market has no Instagram presence , the first agency in each city that shows up consistently owns the feed by default. The database flags exactly who is dark.
Thin reviews are a reputation pitch with urgency built in
A 4.8★ average on a median of 10 reviews is a number one bad month can wreck. Agencies know it, even if they haven't fixed it — the database carries rating and review count on every record so the conversation starts specific.

Methodology
This brief is drawn from the OwnerFlight Florida database (October 2026): licensed home care agencies identified from Florida license records and cross-checked against each agency's public website, Google Business profile, and social presence. Online-booking and Instagram figures reflect what could be found on each agency's public web presence at verification time; records that could not be verified were left blank rather than estimated. The full database — owner/administrator names, phones, license numbers, ratings, booking and social signals, and a 0–100 priority score with a plain-English reason per record — is refreshed weekly, with a weekly Hot 10 of the agencies showing the freshest buying triggers. Florida was the first market. Twenty-three more states are live now.
